verdicts.reason: Line 967 is exactly `const paymentApp = await appStore[...]` with no try/catch; the value awaited is a dynamic import() promise, which can reject where the previous synchronous property access could not. Correct but low-impact, since a rejecting app import mostly means a broken build.

Confirmed by reading the file: `await appStore[...]` (589), `const PaymentService` (594) and `new PaymentService(...)` (595) all sit above the `try { await paymentInstance.refund(...) } catch { handleRefundError(...) }` that starts at 596, so a failure in app resolution or construction bypasses handleRefundError entirely.

index.ts does contain exactly 28 hand-written entries, and the sibling apps.server.generated.ts is machine-generated from the full app list; grepping the repo for tests touching appStore or app-store/index turns up nothing, so nothing keeps the two in sync. Pre-existing condition, but this PR rewrites that list wholesale.

Line 26 is the awaited appStore lookup and there is no try/catch anywhere in handlePayment; the only guard is the `"lib" in paymentApp` shape check, which handles undefined but not a rejected import promise.

Whether an unhandled rejection is swallowed, logged, or fatal depends on the Node version, --unhandled-rejections flag and the Next.js/Vercel process wrapper actually used in production. Settling it needs the deployment's runtime config or an actual run, neither of which is available here.

`const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` then `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)` pushes an already-resolved value, and because the enclosing `.forEach(async ...)` is detached the push typically happens after `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` at line 652 has already run. The line itself is unchanged context inside a hunk this PR modifies.
Line 16 is the awaited appStore lookup; deletePayment has no try/catch and returns `false` only on the shape check, so a rejected dynamic import propagates out of a function typed `Promise<boolean>`.

The PR converts three `forEach((ref) => ...)` callbacks into `forEach(async (ref) => ...)`; forEach discards the returned promises, so the deletes are detached and the surrounding try/catch in the two reschedule.ts files can no longer catch anything (a rejection is now async rather than a synchronous throw). The mention of payment refunds is an overreach — the refund paths are not inside a forEach — but the calendar/video part is accurate at four sites.

getCalendarCredentials stays synchronous and stores the unawaited `getCalendar(credential)` result, so the field named `calendar` now holds `Promise<Calendar | null>`; getConnectedCalendars had to add `const calendar = await item.calendar` at line 47 to compensate. Both current consumers (viewer.tsx, apps/web/pages/api/availability/calendar.ts) go through getConnectedCalendars, so nothing is broken today — it is a naming/clarity hazard.

Read the file: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...) })` inside a try/catch that now catches nothing, and the function proceeds to send reschedule emails without waiting for the deletions. Same shape as vital/lib/reschedule.ts but a separate file needing its own fix.

The premise is wrong: every `import()` in appStore is invoked when index.ts is evaluated, so all module loads are already in flight before getVideoAdapters runs. `await appStore[appName]` awaits an already-pending promise, and `makeVideoApiAdapter(cred)` is synchronous, so the loop does not serialize any loading.
Line 589 is the awaited appStore lookup and it sits above the try block at 596; the same fix (moving the try upward) closes this and c002.

The object literal invokes `import(...)` for all 28 entries at module-evaluation time, storing promises; nothing defers them. Anything that imports appStore therefore kicks off every provider load at once, which defeats the on-demand loading the change is shaped to provide. Thunks (`() => import(...)`) would be the actual fix.

Line 233 is `const calendar = await getCalendar(credential);` in createEvent, outside any try/catch — the function only has `.catch()` handlers on the later `calendar.createEvent(...)` call, so a rejected import escapes before any of that logging runs.

verdicts.reason: Factually true of every await this PR introduces — none of the six `await appStore[...]` sites is wrapped — but the claim names no file, line or function, so it is the weakest possible form of a correct observation.
Same defect as c013 stated differently: the import() calls are evaluated eagerly as object-literal property values, so importing appStore starts every provider load rather than deferring it.

Correct that getCalendarCredentials is still synchronous while its `calendar` field is now `Promise<Calendar | null>`. The 'unchanged type alias' wording is slightly off — consumers use `ReturnType<typeof getCalendarCredentials>`, which is inferred and updates automatically — but the misleading-field-name point stands.

The comment reads `// example: import("./example"),`; neither packages/app-store/example nor packages/app-store/_example exists (the old commented import pointed at `./_example`). Harmless because it is a comment, but the path is wrong and now differs from what it replaced.

Accurate on both halves: today the `await appStore[appName]` inside the for loop awaits promises already started at module evaluation, so it costs nothing; if the eager imports were converted to thunks the same loop would load modules strictly one after another.

Line 15 is the awaited appStore lookup; the function returns null for unknown types via the shape check on line 16 but has no handling for a rejected import promise, and several callers invoke it from detached async callbacks where such a rejection is unhandled.
Answering this needs a build and a deployment to measure chunk sizes and cold-start time; there is no node_modules and no network in this checkout, so nothing can be built or profiled.

Line 128 is `const calendar = await getCalendar(...)` inside the `forEach(async ...)` callback; because forEach drops the callback's promise, a rejection there is unhandled and the enclosing try/catch at 124-139 never sees it. Same defect and same fix as c010.

Confirmed in the file: the callback was changed to `async` by this PR, forEach ignores the returned promise, and execution continues to sendRequestRescheduleEmail without the deletes having completed. Distinct file from wipemycalother, so it needs its own fix.

The described code exists and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` is at line 652 as quoted; the cited line number is off (the push is at 467, 458 is the start of the enclosing block) and the line is unchanged context, but the substance is correct.
Line 128 is the awaited getCalendar inside the detached `forEach(async ...)` callback, so a rejection cannot reach the try/catch wrapping the forEach. Same underlying defect as c023.
